predecessors.name: Gandhāra
predecessors.text: 'Gandhara proper': the Peshawar valley west of the Indus, which Cyrus annexed 'around 535 BCE' (the Gandhara dossier, sa-01-a, loses it in -535)

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: 'In 327 BCE, Alexander the Great conquered Gandhara'; Oxyartes named satrap in 326

ledger.x: c. 535 BCE: Cyrus makes Gandhara a Persian satrapy. 'Around 535 BCE' the Persian king 'organized the conquered territories under the Satrapy of Gandara'; the Gandara page's infobox has 'Cyrus II (c. 535-530 BCE)' as first ruler and its text 'by the later 6th century BCE'; the 518 BCE of other pages is the Behistun…

wars.name: Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley
wars.outcome: Persian victory: 'Cyrus probably went as far as the banks of the Indus river' and 'organized the conquered territories under the Satrapy of Gandara'; the push to the Jhelum came 'around 518 BCE'.

wars.name: Indian campaign of Alexander the Great
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: Gandhara conquered in 327, the Assakenoi 'of Massaga fought him under the command of their queen, Cleophis' and were reduced by stratagem; Alexander 'annexes northwestern India'.

certainty.note: The satrapy is known from inscriptions and Greek authors, not from boundaries; the Indus edge, the Kabul edge and the Taxila line are approximate.
